core_obligations: The small-site parts (proof lines 21123-21130): the restriction pi_{S,*} = i_S^{-1} is a right adjoint of the exact functor pi_S^{-1}, so it preserves injectives by the Homology lemma and K-injectives by the Derived Categories lemma, giving (1)(b) and (2)(b).

The big-site parts, first proof (proof lines 21132-21141): i_f^{-1} is a right adjoint of the exact functor i_{f,!}, whose construction is in Topologies and Modules on Sites and whose exactness is proved in Modules on Sites, so the same two lemmas give (1)(a) and (2)(a).

The big-site parts, second proof (proof lines 21142-21149): factor i_f = i_T composed with f_big; since f_big is a localisation, its pullback preserves injectives and K-injectives, and applying the already-proved small-site parts to i_T^{-1} concludes.

The counterexample for modules (proof lines 21151-21169): over S = Spec(Z) the multiplication map 2 : O_S -> O_S is injective as O_S-modules but its pullback to the big site is not injective, as evaluating on Spec(F_2) shows; embedding O into an injective O-module I on the big site gives a diagram whose dotted arrow cannot exist, because by adjunction it would factor the injection alpha through the non-injective map, so I|_{S_etale} is not injective as an O_S-module.
proof_roadmap: Get (1)(b) and (2)(b) from right adjointness of the restriction to the small site.
Get (1)(a) and (2)(a) either from right adjointness of i_{f,!} or by factoring through the localisation morphism and reusing the small-site parts.
Disprove the module statement by the multiplication-by-2 counterexample over Spec(Z).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that injective and K-injective abelian sheaves on the big etale site stay injective, respectively K-injective, when restricted to the small etale site or pulled back along an object, and that the corresponding statements for modules fail (statement lines 21101-21120). The positive parts (proof lines 21122-21149) are formal from right adjointness of exact functors, with two independent proofs for the pullback case; the negative part (proof lines 21151-21169) is an explicit counterexample over Spec(Z): multiplication by 2 is injective but its pullback is not, and the absence of the dotted arrow exhibits a non-injective restriction of an injective module. H2: formal adjunction arguments plus one explicit counterexample.
